headline: Medium risk: shared allowlisted egress and data-warehouse access create leakage and cascading-error pathways; no direct injection channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel, filesystem bridge, or clipboard/MCP path is documented between dbt-core and nuwa-skill. dbt-core only shows allowlisted network egress and data-warehouse API calls; nuwa-skill exposes no I/O surfaces. With no ingestion path, prompt injection is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the agents, injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not pipe one agent's raw text into the other.
If a bridge is added, require provenance tags on all transferred content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and has allowlisted egress, while nuwa-skill has no declared data classes or I/O surfaces. The pair does not show a shared workspace or authenticated principal, so leakage is not evidenced; however, if dbt outputs warehouse-derived content into nuwa-skill, sensitive data could be exposed through its egress path.
conditions: IF dbt-core is configured to pass warehouse rows or query results into nuwa-skill, leakage risk increases.
IF both agents are run under the same account with a shared workspace, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Run each agent under a separate OS account.
Disable unnecessary logging of prompts and outputs.
Review any allowlisted destinations before enabling transfers.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dbt-core can call a data warehouse and nuwa-skill has no declared write, network, or concurrency surfaces. There is no documented overlapping mutable resource, so direct conflict is not shown. Uncertainty remains because nuwa-skill's concurrency model is empty; if it writes to the same warehouse or shared state, contention could appear.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill is granted write access to the same warehouse objects as dbt-core, conflict risk increases.
IF both agents modify the same shared files or tables without locking, conflict risk increases.
mitigations: Use explicit locking or job serialization.
Limit nuwa-skill to read-only access unless needed.

D_cascading_error.rationale: dbt-core can produce warehouse-derived outputs that nuwa-skill may consume, but nuwa-skill's verification behavior is undocumented. Because the interaction pathway is inferred rather than observed, uncertainty pushes this above low: if nuwa-skill treats dbt output as authoritative, downstream actions or reports can propagate errors across multiple work products.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill consumes dbt-core outputs without an explicit validation step, cascading error risk is present.
IF nuwa-skill triggers reports or actions from dbt-generated facts, errors can propagate downstream.
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents.
Require nuwa-skill to cite source queries or checksums.
Flag dbt outputs as untrusted until verified.
Sample-check a few outputs before downstream use.

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and has allowlisted egress, but no residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for nuwa-skill. Because only one agent clearly handles regulated data classes, the compliance pathway is limited and not evidenced as a breach; the other agent is not cited for a specific mismatch because none is declared.
conditions: IF warehouse data includes regulated personal data and nuwa-skill is deployed in a jurisdiction or retention regime that differs from the warehouse policy, compliance risk increases.
IF dbt-core outputs are retained longer than the source warehouse policy, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Confirm the data class before sharing outputs.
Align retention settings across both tools.
Document the processing location for any exported data.
